71b4969829.q: What problem did Nancy Yen identify that led to creating Omi Life and OmiBox?
71b4969829.a: Nancy noticed that her son, who was small for his age and accustomed to eating hot food at home, was coming home from preschool with uneaten lunches because he had to eat only cold foods like sandwiches at school. She realized that kids lack variety in traditional packed lunch options and are highly motivated to skip eating to go play, so she designed OmiBox to allow parents to pack hot and cold foods together in one visible compartment layout that keeps meals appealing and encourages children to finish eating.

edf8440f0c.q: How does OmiBox solve the problem of lost container lids in school lunches?
edf8440f0c.a: OmiBox features only one hinged lid that cannot be lost, though the thermos component does have a separate lid. Nancy anticipated this problem and designed the product so that all components are sold as spare parts at low prices on their website, allowing customers to refresh or replace lids, gaskets, and other parts without discarding the entire box, promoting durability and sustainability.

5bbe0d3d88.q: How can entrepreneurs identify blind spot opportunities in everyday life?
5bbe0d3d88.a: According to Nancy, problems entrepreneurs are most sensitive to are those they face in their own everyday life and that affect their friends in the same life stage. She emphasizes that parenting has many pain points making it a rich area for discovery, and recommends starting by identifying inconveniences in your own community before expanding to problems outside your personal experience by talking to and observing people who work around pain points they accept as normal.
